summary: Pierhead light at the end of Cleveland's east breakwater: temporary light 1888, iron tower lit 1911, privately owned since a 2008 auction.

structures.note: Cylindrical iron tower 25 ft tall with a fifth-order acetylene light (LighthouseFriends). The record says wood, 9.5 m.
Formal tower on the eastern breakwater with a five-day lens-lantern first shown 20 Aug 1897. Sources do not say whether the 1911 tower replaced it.

lens.where: Fourth order from 1912 (LighthouseFriends); current optic not described in sources read

access.note: Privately owned since the 2008 auction. The lighthouse is privately owned; grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Private owner since the 2008 online auction (2009 magazine report named the buyer as a New York City restoration company)

events.note: Cleveland life-saving crew rescued the crew of the barge John T. Johnson off the east pier on 11-12 Nov 1884; the whole crew won gold medals
Temporary mast light on the eastern breakwater, first shown 8 Sept 1888

Board 1891-1892 entry 1103: a boathouse built in front of the beacon on the Cleveland East Pier, projecting 4 feet over the pier, to shelter the keeper's boat used to signal the west pierhead light; the boathouse is not confirmed as this light's
Steamer Detroit collided with a schooner and was forced against the east pier; guards injured the foundation sills of the pierhead beacon (Board 1893)
East Pier light moved about 121 ft southward to the outer end of the new concrete pier (Board 1896-1897)
Formal tower on the eastern breakwater; five-day lens-lantern lit 20 Aug 1897
Congress appropriated funds on 27 May 1908 for the new east breakwater pierhead light ($12,000 requested)
Cylindrical iron tower 25 ft tall; fifth-order acetylene flashing light commissioned at the opening of navigation
Changed from fifth-order to fourth-order light
Temporarily removed so the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers could repair the pier
Declared excess by the Coast Guard in May 2007 and offered at no cost to eligible entities; no qualified owner came forward
Online auction closed 2 Dec 2008; lighthouse sold for $10,000
Cleveland Magazine (Aug 2009, as cited by LighthouseFriends) named the buyer as Artisan Restoration Group; plan to install a composting toilet and rent the light and pier to boaters

27 June 1911: the east breakwater west-end light changed to flashing white and shown from a 25 ft square steel pyramidal tower that replaced a taller tower on wooden legs (LighthouseFriends). Relation to the pierhead tower not stated.

keepers.name: Reed
keepers.note: 'Lightkeeper Reed' in the 1884 Life-Saving Service report ('Customs Inspector Bates and Lightkeeper Reed, who were on the pier'); 'Assistant Lighthouse Keeper Reed' in LighthouseFriends. First name not given. The USLHS roster for the Cleveland East Pierhead Beacon lists no keepers.

Collided with a schooner and was forced against the east pier; guards injured the foundation sills of the pierhead beacon and put the beacon itself in peril; foundation repaired. Year inferred from the fiscal-1893 report (scanned text prints 1802).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's first years conflict. The 1831 date belongs to a USLHS beacon record for a 'Cleveland East Pierhead Beacon' that no longer exists, whose coordinates (41.5037, -81.6833) are about 2.7 km east of this pier (41.5102, -81.7155). LighthouseFriends dates a temporary mast light to 1888 and the present tower to 1911. The sources read do not link the 1831 beacon to this pier.

The record says a source calls the structure gone while OpenStreetMap maps it. LighthouseFriends describes the tower as standing and privately owned, and the USLHS record for the 1831 beacon says that beacon no longer exists. The present tower appears to stand, but no source read after 2009 confirms its condition.

notes_for_editor: WRONG ROSTER ATTACHED, NOT USED: the record's USLHS lookup matched 'Cleveland Harbor Main Entrance' (https://archives.uslhs.org/places/cleveland-harbor-main-entrance; roster https://archives.uslhs.org/general/showPeople/3450; 61 lines, 1911-1965, including Frederick Thomas Hatch as principal keeper 1911-1914) by name and position. That record is the WEST Pierhead light: its alternate name is 'Cleveland West Pierhead', its foundation is 'CONCRETE (WEST PIERHEAD)' and its focal height is 67 ft. It is not this station, so no roster lines or person slugs are attached here. The name-based match should be corrected. IDENTITY: LighthouseFriends says the Main Entrance and East Breakwater lights were activated in 1911 as a pair; the LighthouseFriends page for the East Breakwater matches this record's coordinates (41.5102, -81.7155). Confirm the USCG LLNR (7-4165) against the Light List before the story goes live. TWO 1911 TOWERS: LighthouseFriends describes a cylindrical iron pierhead tower (25 ft) and, separately, a 25 ft square steel tower for the east breakwater west-end light on 27 June 1911; the story reports both and does not link them. FLOOD TELEGRAM REMOVED: the 1884 Life-Saving Service report's telegram to Keeper Goodwin and the 3 a.m. departure on the 12th belong to the February 1884 Ohio River flood relief (Cincinnati and Covington), not to the 11 November barge rescue; the story no longer uses them. HILL LIGHT REMOVED: the Board's 'hill light on the east side of Cleveland Harbor' (discontinued 1892, lens to Braddock Point) is a different structure and is not in the story. OTHER NEWS, NOT USED: Hoodline (7 Aug 2026, https://hoodline.com/2026/08/cleveland-s-offshore-lighthouse-is-up-for-grabs-again-and-a-lakewood-man-wants-it/) reports on the WEST Pierhead tower (67 ft cast iron), a GSA transfer notice and a failed 2023 auction; it is not this station. No 2026 source for the East Pierhead was found. RECORD VALUES NOT CONFIRMED: characteristic 'Iso G 6s' and range 6.1 nm are not confirmed by any source read; the record's wood 9.5 m tower conflicts with LighthouseFriends' iron tower. OCR: the 1893 report prints the Detroit collision date as 'November 19, 1802'; the report is for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1893, so November 1892 is the only fitting date and the story gives 1892 with a footnote; scan page 202 confirmed by page index (scan 192 also matches the same text). SCAN PAGES CONFIRMED: 1891-92 scan 179 and 189; 1896-97 scan 409; LSS 1884 scan 151 (also scan 150 in the lifesavingservic10unitrich copy). KEEPERS: no roster for this light was found. The only lighthouse keeper named is 'Lightkeeper Reed' (LSS) / 'Assistant Lighthouse Keeper Reed' (LighthouseFriends). Keeper Charles C. Goodwin was a life-saving station keeper. CURRENT STATUS: LighthouseFriends is undated and reports the 2008 auction and 2009 buyer as the latest events; the owner, condition and any plans after 2009 are unconfirmed. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it with short quotations only. Confidence low.
